programme: A MECOM–SMAD7–ID2/TSC22D1 TGF-β/BMP–Smad negative-feedback circuit. MECOM's target set in this network includes SMAD7 directly, matching MECOM/EVI1's documented role elsewhere as a transcriptional inducer of SMAD7. SMAD7 in turn targets SMAD3, TGFB1, ACVR1B and SMURF2 — the canonical machinery by which inhibitory SMAD7 recruits SMURF2 to degrade the TGF-β/activin receptor and shut the pathway off. ID2 (targeting BMP4 and INHBA) and TSC22D1 (a TGF-β-inducible early-response gene, targeting TSC2/CDKN1A) sit downstream as the pathway's canonical readout genes. Together this is a self-contained brake-and-gauge module for TGF-β/BMP–Smad signalling, not a generic label.
role_in_a: In lower-grade glioma, TGF-β/Smad signalling is a well-characterised driver of invasiveness, EMT-like transition and microenvironment immunosuppression. SMAD7 is specifically reported as a regulated node of this pathway in glioma cells, with its repression by miR-132 or by the TGF-β1/miR-205/miR-195 axis potentiating oncogenic TGF-β output (PMID 25983322, 27574009). MECOM's induction of SMAD7 seen in this network would set how tightly that brake is applied to tumour TGF-β signalling.
role_in_b: In Parkinson's disease, glial TGF-β/BMP–Smad output is known to support dopaminergic neuron survival and restrain neuroinflammation. The ID2 locus, via its antisense transcript ID2-AS1, has been shown to modulate neuronal injury in the MPP+ toxin model of PD (PMID 34050453), consistent with BMP/TGF-β-responsive gene output shaping dopaminergic vulnerability.
shared_axis: A glioma cell and a dopaminergic neuron–glia unit both depend on correctly tuned TGF-β/BMP–Smad output — for growth arrest and immune control in the tumour, for trophic and anti-inflammatory support in the midbrain. A shift toward this MECOM/SMAD7-driven feedback brake would simultaneously blunt TGF-β-restrained tumour behaviour in LGG and blunt TGF-β/BMP-dependent neuroprotection in PD: the same molecular brake, a tissue-appropriate consequence in each.
reasoning: The module is nameable on its own terms — the network itself places SMAD7 under MECOM and shows SMAD7 carrying the canonical SMURF2/TGFB1/ACVR1B machinery, and SMAD7 (in LGG) and ID2 (in PD) are each independently placed in one disease by retrieved papers. But no retrieved source states the LGG–PD connection itself, MECOM and TSC22D1 carry no literature placement in either disease here, and concordance across the 279 comparisons is moderate (92–126, i.e. ~33–45%) rather than near-universal, so the cross-disease link rests on pathway reasoning rather than documentation.
support: PMID 25983322 — miR-132 represses SMAD7 to potentiate TGF-β pathway activation in glioma cells, placing SMAD7 in LGG; PMID 27574009 — TGF-β1/miR-205/miR-195 axis regulates SMAD7 in glioma, placing SMAD7 in LGG; PMID 34050453 — knockdown of the ID2-locus antisense transcript ID2-AS1 alleviates MPP+-induced neuronal injury in a PD toxin model, placing the ID2 locus in PD (via its antisense RNA, not ID2 protein directly).
how_to_falsify: In an LGG cell line, knock down MECOM and measure SMAD7 promoter occupancy and transcript level (ChIP-qPCR, RT-qPCR); if MECOM loss does not reduce SMAD7 expression, the proposed MECOM→SMAD7 edge underlying the shared brake is wrong. Separately, in an MPP+ or AAV-α-synuclein dopaminergic neuron/microglia model, titrate SMAD7 overexpression against BMP/TGF-β-driven ID2 and TSC22D1 induction and against neuron survival; if raising SMAD7 fails to suppress ID2/TSC22D1 induction or fails to worsen neuronal loss, the neuroprotection arm of the shared axis is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|brain, not brain|brain — the PD side of this network is likely built substantially from peripheral blood rather than midbrain tissue, so any TGF-β/BMP–Smad signal recovered there is at best a peripheral echo of a CNS process. Concordance for the carrying factors runs only 92–126 of 279 comparisons (~33–45%), and only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the whole analysis, so the circuit is recurrent but not dominant. MECOM and TSC22D1 have no Open Targets or literature placement in either disease here — their inclusion rests on known TGF-β-superfamily biology (MECOM/EVI1 as a documented SMAD7 inducer; TSC22D1 as a documented TGF-β-inducible gene) plus this network's own MECOM→SMAD7 edge, not on retrieved disease evidence, so treat them as plausible scaffolding rather than confirmed nodes. NR4A2 carries the strongest disease-specific literature of any factor in this list (PD dopaminergic identity, one LGG hub-gene paper) but its targets (TH, SLC6A3, DBH, NGF) show no overlap with the MECOM/SMAD7/ID2/TSC22D1 target sets, so it was deliberately left out rather than folded in to inflate this account. JARID2 (highest recurrence, 142/279) and NR1H3 (131/279) were excluded despite topping the ranking because neither has any disease association or usable literature connection recorded — a reminder that recurrence rank and mechanistic relevance are not the same thing. NOTCH1, STAT2 and other canonical brain/immune regulators were removed as tissue-generic, so their absence reflects that filter, not an oversight.
